note: Strings a mechanical rename must not rewrite. Held by test/rewrite-exceptions.test.ts.

exceptions.reason: Two command transcripts pasted with the output they actually produced. Editing a command so it no longer matches the output beneath it fabricates evidence — in the one document that exists to argue against doing exactly that.
The Decision statement records the rename itself. A decision that names both sides of a change cannot have one side rewritten without becoming a different decision.

The migration section tells a reader where the repository moved from, and warns that the old name is unclaimed and could be squatted. Both sentences are about the old name; rewriting them deletes their subject.

A dated amendment note citing issue #8 by the URL as it stood that day. Weaker than the others — GitHub redirects, so rewriting it would be harmless rather than destructive. Listed because a guard needs the complete picture, and because a reader deserves to know which exceptions are load-bearing and which are merely old.

Pasted shell transcripts in which the developer's own clone directory was named that. The path is a fact about the machine the commands ran on, not a reference to the repository, so rewriting it would misreport what was actually executed.
A doc comment quoting the same symlink command as it was run. Same reasoning as the transcript above; this one sits in a test file, where a reader is most likely to copy it verbatim.

The agent-facing identity note tells a reader which superseded string this manifest is about. A guard that forced that sentence to name nothing would make the manifest harder to find than the prose it replaced — and this entry exists because the guard flagged the sentence as it was being written.
